Subject: Dedicated GPU recommendations for document ingestion pipeline

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As mentioned, Olive is evaluating a Dedicated capacity purchase for our real-time document ingestion + QA assistant. Our key constraints are:
- 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for single-doc queries (average doc size ~ 4k tokens)
- Peak concurrent sessions ~ 220, typical steady-state ~ 80
- Some workflows include multi-document context windows (up to 32k tokens) for cross-doc search/QA

We're trying to understand whether we should commit to H100-heavy pools, A100 (80GB) mixes, or use L4 for cheaper low-cost tails. We've attached a small sampled workload trace and the SOW draft. Can you advise on SKU tradeoffs including memory headroom, latency, batching behavior, and fallback strategy? Also curious about cost delta for Reserved vs burst usage.

Attached: olive_workload_trace_20270409.jsonl, Olive_SOW_initial_draft.pdf

—Sam

Elliot — thanks. Quick answers inline:
1) Model mix: production will be an optimized 13B family for latency-sensitive routes, with ~20% of requests routed to a 70B quality tier for complex QA. Both use a KV-cache pattern (user session history + document embeddings cached).
2) Long-context (32k) will be a separate route using a 70B long-context variant; infrequent (~5% of requests) but high memory.
3) Procurement preference is to buy ~70% reserved if performance/cost tradeoff is favorable; we can accept some burst in cloud for spikes.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: FW: Olive Systems — Dedicated GPU recommendations — need SKU guidance

Elliot / Neha / Kim —

Quick recommendation (summary first):
- Mix: 40% H100-80GB, 50% A100-80GB, 10% L4 (burst/low-cost tail and embedding offload).
- Rationale: H100s for pinned long-context 70B capacity and for latency-sensitive 13B hot paths with large KV caches; A100-80 for the bulk quantized 13B throughput (good memory and throughput balance); L4s as dense, cheap slots for non-latency-critical embedding and batched offline work and for absorbing low-priority inference.
- Reserved vs burst: Target 70% reserved on A100 + H100 mix, keep a 30% burst pool on cloud using L4-heavy instances to save committed spend while preserving hard SLOs via routing rules (route 70B long-context to reserved H100s always).

Detailed notes:
1) Memory headroom: 70B long-context at 32k strongly favors H100-80GB (or multi-GPU model-shard with NVLink if Olive wants to avoid H100). Running a 70B 32k with quantization and KV caching still consumes large resident memory (model weights + activations + KV). H100's memory bandwidth and larger on-package memory for sparse ops will reduce tail latency. If Olive cannot accept H100, A100-80GB with careful model sharding + reduced batch concurrency is possible but will increase latency and complexity.

2) 13B optimized path: For single-doc 4k requests, quantized A100-80GB gives best cost/perf. A100 sustains higher concurrency for 13B and yields predictable latency when combined with continuous batching and KV prefix caching. H100 gives slightly better per-token latency but at ~2x cost premium. Recommend putting hot 13B session-affinity state on A100s with KV cache pinned to the instance; however, for the top 20% quality traffic (70B), reserve H100 slots to avoid noisy neighbor interference.

3) L4 role: L4 is a cost-efficient option for embedding workloads, reranking, and lower-SLA inference routes. Use L4 as a flexible spillover for batch/embeddings and for burst capacity in cloud. L4 cannot host 70B long-context without significant degradation; do not route 70B traffic to L4.

4) Fallback and routing policy:
- Primary routing: 70B long-context -> H100 reserved pool (strict).
- Primary routing: 13B latency-sensitive -> A100 reserved pool (preferred); if saturated, overflow to H100 reserved (if available) before L4 burst to avoid latency cliffs.
- Low-priority/embeddings -> L4 burst/spot.
- Enforce per-model concurrency caps and per-token budgets to protect 99p SLO.

5) Cost delta (very rough):
- Baseline (all reserved A100-equivalent): $X/month (proprietary calc)
- Proposed mixed reserved (70% reserved split A100+H100) + 30% L4 burst: ~15–25% lower committed monthly cost vs fully H100-reserved, with <10% SLO risk if routing is enforced. Exact numbers depend on cloud instance pricing and Olive's reserved discount level; Kimberly can provide precise delta.

6) Operational considerations:
- Benchmark representative 32k and 4k flows on H100 and A100 hardware before final commit.
- Pin KV caches to physical instances for session-affinity to avoid cache misses on overflow.
- Prepare a short failover playbook: in case H100 capacity reduced, system gracefully downgrades new long-context requests to queued background processing with a clear SLA to users.

Attachments recommended to send back: a 1-page SKU mix table and an ops checklist for long-context model sharding.

Happy to sketch the table — Kim, can you take a stab at the cost delta numbers and a short table I can send to Sam?

—Dev Patel

Sam —

Thanks for the details. Short version of our recommended Dedicated mix (based on your profile):
- 40% H100-80GB: reserved slots for 70B long-context and headroom for top-quality traffic (5–20% of requests).
- 50% A100-80GB: reserved capacity for quantized 13B hot paths (primary latency pool for 4k doc queries).
- 10% L4: burst/low-cost pool for embeddings, reranking, and overflow batch jobs.

Why this configuration?
- H100: necessary for predictable 32k 70B latency and memory headroom; minimizes tail latency for long-context requests.
- A100: best cost/throughput for quantized 13B; supports session-affinity and KV cache resident on instance to meet your 99p 250ms SLO for 4k requests.
- L4: cost-effective absorbent for non-latency-critical work and burst; do not route 70B long-context to L4.

Routing/fallback plan (high level):
1) Always route 70B long-context to H100 reserved pool.
2) Route 13B latency routes to A100 reserved; overflow to H100 reserved.
3) Use L4 pool only for embeddings, reranks, and queued batch when A100/H100 are saturated.
4) Keep 70% of the A100+H100 capacity reserved (as you prefer). We'll set up per-model concurrency caps and KV pinning to protect the 99p SLO.

Next steps:
- Kimberly will send a short cost delta estimate and a 1-page SKU table comparing estimated monthly committed vs mixed-burst economics.
- If this looks good, we can produce an SOW and a pilot run on A100+H100 for 2 weeks to validate the 99p numbers against your trace.

I've attached the high-level proposal PDF and the workload trace back for continuity. Let us know if you want to jump on a 30m call tomorrow.

Best,
